[LGRA.21.2] **`test` is a reserved word** ([LLEX.9.5]), promoted to keyword
meaning at the start of a top-level declaration — the same position-promotion
`series` takes. Recognition is positional; reservation is not. An author must
not name a binding, slot, `const`, schema or rule `test`, and the compiler must
refuse one that is.

The heads inside a test body — `inputs`, `responses`, `produces`, `until`, `at`,
`for`, `response`, `activated`, `emitted`, `published`, `retracted`, `recorded`,
`called`, `cached`, `cache_deleted`, `logged`, `wm`, `has`, `count`, `empty` —
are promoted only in their body positions and reserved everywhere, as is
`never`, the oracle-polarity prefix on `test_assertion`. `no`, in `no response`,
is the same reserved word the rule surface uses.
